title: Error Origins Chronicle and Probe Wires
summary: A sketch + working notes for a chronological 'Error Origins Chronicle' and interactive 'Probe Card' surfaces. Goal: make it fast for an engineer or SRE to move from a high-level alert (timeout/5xx/model-error) to a small set of actionable probes and hypotheses they can run from the console without leaving the incident flow.
problem_statement: Current console shows flat lists of failed requests and raw traces. Investigators still need to stitch network logs, model variant, routing policy, and prefix/KV cache context. We want a single timeline with contextual probes and suggested reruns to reduce mean time to mitigation and make root-cause hypotheses explicit.
objectives: Unify multi-source signals into a single chronological narrative (request -> routing -> model -> runtime -> infra)
Provide one-click probe actions (replay with different model, flush cache + replay, run vs. canary model, capture full token-level diff)
Expose a small set of hypothesis templates and telemetry needed to confirm/disprove each hypothesis
audience: Oncall SREs, product engineers debugging latency/5xx/model errors, solutions engineers investigating customer incidents
proposed_views: 1) Chronicle Timeline: horizontal time axis that layers events (client request, gateway latencies, routing decision, model inference start/end, GPU/memory thrash events, infra autoscaler events). Each event node is clickable and opens a compact inspector. 2) Probe Card Rail: a right-side rail that lists auto-suggested probes (replay w/ same model, replay w/ quantized variant, replay without prefix cache, replay with throttled batch size, run synthetic with smaller input). Each probe has expected quick metric impact and confidence level. 3) Hypothesis Deck: a top banner area where the investigator can pin up to 3 hypotheses; each hypothesis links to probes and shows required telemetry to validate. 4) Evidence Panel: bottom panel with aggregated logs, sampled token diffs, network captures, and correlated traces from other regions/replicas.
wireframe_components: Chronicle Timeline (compact stacked lanes: client/gateway, router/policy, model runtime, infra/host) — hover reveals quick stats
Probe Card (list of suggested probes with run button + small cost estimate + estimated time)
Evidence Panel (collapsible: logs, token-diff viewer, heatmap of latency vs token position)
Compact Inspector (for any node: shows 1-line summary, request metadata, model version, token count, KV cache hits, GPU utilization snapshot)
Action History (chronicle of probes run during this investigation with outcomes and links to generated artifacts)
Share / Attach button to create a ticket with current hypothesis and artifacts attached
interaction_flows: Typical flow: alert -> open chronicle for the request -> click 'Router decision' node -> console suggests 3 probes (replay with fallback model, replay flush-cache, replay routing-only) -> investigator runs 'replay flush-cache' -> outcome shows token-diff and latency change -> pin hypothesis 'cache staleness' and run 2nd probe 'replay with canary model' if needed -> if confirmed, create remediation (route update) via quick deploy action. Keep investigator context (pinned hypothesis) across probes and allow rollback of probes to save cost.
mockup_notes: Visual affordances: use color-coded event types (red=error, amber=high-latency, blue=info). Probe Card buttons: primary (Run probe), secondary (preview cost/time). Mini-token-diff viewer: show aligned tokens with highlight on divergent tokens and a small 'confidence delta' score. For time-critical alerts, show pre-populated probe set optimized for speed (1-2 probes under 30s). Persist last successful probe for the request to avoid duplicate runs.

metrics_and_telemetry_needed: per-request timeline with timestamps for router/model/runtime/infra events
KV cache hit/miss counts and prefix lengths
GPU/CPU utilization at inference start/end (1s granularity)
per-probe cost estimate and actual run time
token-level probabilities or confidence deltas (redacted for PII)
open_questions: How do we rate-limit probes to prevent accidental load generation?
What guardrails are needed for private deployments with air-gapped telemetry?
Should probes run under a namespace's dedicated capacity or the investigator's sandbox quota?
What is the minimum data retention window required to make Chronicle useful (7d vs 30d)?
